title: ID-JAG: a user's identity at an app whose IdP you do not control
lede: The exchange returns an identity assertion grant that the gateway redeems at the application's own issuer. The deck claims no shared credential and no re-consent. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

edges.label: exchange for an ID-JAG, aud = partner issuer

steps.title: The agent calls the gateway
steps.what: The call carries the caller's token, from the IdP the gateway trusts.

steps.title: Gateway asks for a grant
steps.what: RFC 8693 exchange with a requested token type of an identity assertion grant.

steps.title: IdP issues the grant
steps.what: A short-lived JWT naming the user and the partner issuer as its audience.

steps.title: Redeem at the app's issuer
steps.what: The grant is presented to the issuer the app trusts. The lab sends no client credential on this leg (it omits client authentication).

steps.title: Issuer verifies the grant
steps.what: In this lab it trusts that IdP (set up in advance, the lab's model) and checks signature, audience, expiry and that the grant was not used before: the lab's rules, not the deck's list.

steps.title: Partner issuer mints a token
steps.what: The user's identity is now expressed in a token from the app's own issuer. The lab models no consent step (the deck claims no re-consent).

steps.title: Gateway calls the app
steps.what: The app validates its own issuer's token as usual.
